## findings
**T1-1 — SOURCE-TASK RED (persona contradicts the user tool contract; stale after r1).** Persona: "you pass the client reference number, the engagement reference number and the value change the desk tells you, unchanged, and if asked you read back the change order number the confirmation shows." Tool: `sign_restart_change_order_602c3012(ctx, customer_id, change_order_number, value_delta_usd)` — no engagement argument, change_order_number required as input. Consequence: a simulator following its script passes `project_engagement_id` (unexpected argument) and omits the change order number, so the GT call `{customer_id, change_order_number: CO-044310-03, value_delta_usd: 8191.34}` is reached only if the simulator departs from its own lines; the persona also treats the CO number as an output. Affected: 1.json user_scenario. Root cause per design_rationale "[Revisions] r1 … tool signature: customer_id, change_order_number, value_delta_usd" (XF#22 stale text).

**T1-2 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (XF#20).** (1) `managed_agreements/f75a407f…` ClearPath Professional, 24-month term, 120 seats, signed 2025-05-12: `managed_signing_terms` invoices an onboarding fee of 75.00 × 120 = 9,000.00 on the signing date unless the term is ≥ 36 months — no managed_onboarding_fee row. (2) Monthly fees absent for 2025-08…2025-12 (agreement live 2025-07-01); 2025-10/11/12 lie inside the twelve-month window of clearpath_standing ("ClearPath billing shows … late fees posted in the twelve months before the re-pricing date"), whose count of 1 then rests on absent rows. (3) No managed_service_requests intake row. Affected: 1.json initial_state.

**T1-3 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (demonstration of `_difficulty.md` C11 on this world).** This task's hold_length and hold_span ladders are unreal: probe on SOW-044310 (on hold 2026-05-29, Major, max 90): resumption after 179 days → re-pricing block 9,868.16 and remob span 5,500.00; after 180 days → 9,471.40 and 4,166.67. The task scores the middle tier of two ladders whose top tier charges a longer pause less.

**T1-4 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (demonstration of C12).** This Major engagement's fee_basis: the gold middle tier gives 2.5 % × 8,191.34 = 204.78 against the 350.00 flat fee an ordinary change order of the same size pays, and the ladder falls from 500.00 at |delta| 19,999.99 to 350.00 at 20,000.00.

**T1-5 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (demonstration of C13).** The gold M2 invoice re-bills milestone 1's credit: true-up 60 % × 256,000 − (48,000 + 49,296) = 56,304.00; with M1 billed at its uncredited 49,920.00 the true-up would be 55,680.00 — the 624.00 difference is exactly M1's 1.25 % credit, taken back before the new 2.5 % credit is applied. Reading "credit … taken off" as a reduction of what the client pays gives 55,680.00 × 0.975 = 54,288.00, against the rule-as-computed 54,896.40.

**T1-6 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (demonstration of C15).** After the gold sequence the engagement row still shows contract_value_usd 256,000.00 and change_order_count 2 while CO-044310-03 is signed at +8,191.34; inherited base "A signed change order changes contract_value_usd by its value delta" (event fields "contract_value_usd: New contract value., change_order_count: Incremented.") requires 264,191.34 and 3. The scored terminal state contradicts an in-force base provision.

Observations: O-a the earlier 34-day April hold behind the 2026-05-06 remobilization fee (2,500.00) is recorded nowhere but that fee row (the engagement stores only its latest hold); O-b DR multi-source labels on managed_rate/continuity are inaccurate (no consequence); O-c the C2/C3/C4/C5/C14 charter defects do not move this task's numbers (CO-03 registered on resumed_date and the latest signed; no same-day CO-fee tie; fee non-zero).
